solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cross about Scottish inventor being guest announcer (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in turned about, facing the other way, so the word for cross is written backwards

blocks.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix; turned about it gives DOOR
Alexander Graham Bell, born in Edinburgh

annotation.surface: An irritable Scottish inventor is asked to announce the guests at a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the noun rood, a church crucifix.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful descriptive definition: the device rings to tell you a visitor is at the door, doing a herald's job.

entries.clue: Shot 500 sheep (4)

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: Five hundred sheep are shot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a verb about culling a flock; it is the noun, a small drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the drinks sense: a small measure of spirits, especially whisky in Scotland.

entries.clue: Film at sea, perhaps type to include river (2,3,10)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: 'perhaps' flags an example: font is one instance of type, not a synonym
indicatorNotes.to include: to include something is to take it inside, so FONT holds R within its letters

blocks.note: a font is a set of type
R = river, placed inside FONT to make FRONT

annotation.surface: A note on a film set at sea, and what typeface to use for its river scenes.
annotation.walkthrough: On the Waterfront is the 1954 Marlon Brando film about New Jersey dockworkers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is the title of a famous film.

entries.clue: Data presentation showing reduction initially in pub opening hours (3,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the first letter of 'reduction' is used
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another: R sits inside the word for opening

blocks.note: first letter of reduction, inside GAP

annotation.surface: A chart showing a cut in pub opening hours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pub opening hours' reads as one phrase, but it splits into three separate pieces: pub, opening, hours.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a chart of bars of varying length is one way of presenting data.

entries.clue: Component of basic education adopted by spare master (5)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: a child adopted by a family is taken into it, so R is taken into the word for spare

blocks.note: one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

annotation.surface: Some part of basic schooling is taken on by a spare teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a teacher, but here it is the verb: to master a skill.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, verb for verb: to master a subject is to get it thoroughly into your head.

entries.clue: Computer part used in US city work (6)

indicatorNotes.used in: a thing used in a job goes into it, so PT is put inside the city and the work

annotation.surface: A computer component is being used in some work in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Computer part' looks like one phrase; the definition is 'Computer' alone, and 'part' is the abbreviation PT.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one type of portable computer.

entries.clue: TV host’s job curtailed after article (6)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: 'curtailed' literally means cut short at the tail, so the job word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following in order, so the shortened job comes behind the article

blocks.note: CHORE, a job, without its tail

annotation.surface: A television presenter's job is cut short after a newspaper article.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'article' is the grammar word, not a newspaper piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A media sense, mainly American: the anchor is the presenter who holds a news broadcast together.

entries.clue: Retired copper with personnel in support restrain New York man (10,5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places personnel within the support, so HR goes inside TEE

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
HR = human resources, placed in TEE
to pen is to shut in
a chess man is a piece

annotation.surface: A retired policeman teams up with staff to hold down a New Yorker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired copper' reads as an ex-policeman, but it is a coin taken out of use. The threepenny piece was an old British coin worth three pennies, withdrawn in 1971.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on copper: a policeman in the surface, but also a low-value coin, and this one is retired from circulation.

entries.clue: Sea creature: plan to net one going over western sound (5,5)

indicatorNotes.to net: to net is to catch in a net, so the plan word traps I inside it
indicatorNotes.going over: in a down clue, what goes over something sits above it, so PILOT comes before W and HALE

blocks.note: sound = healthy, as in 'hale and hearty'

annotation.surface: A marine animal, with a scheme to catch one crossing a western strait.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests a stretch of sea, fitting the surface; it means healthy.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the pilot whale, a large oceanic dolphin, is one kind of sea creature.

entries.clue: Question posed in shock English musical number (4,4)

indicatorNotes.posed in: a question posed in something is put inside it, so HOW goes within the word for shock

blocks.note: how? is a question word, placed in STUN

annotation.surface: A question is asked in a startling English musical number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock' reads as a noun in the surface; it is the verb stun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a number is a song in a stage show, and a song from a musical is exactly this.

entries.clue: Later events ruined that frame (9)

indicatorNotes.ruined: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters of 'that frame' fall into a new order

annotation.surface: Something that happened afterwards spoiled a picture frame.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Later events' looks like it might be wordplay; it is the definition, and the fodder is the last two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the aftermath is what comes after an event, usually a bad one.

entries.clue: Ocean feature ruined at the outset, covered in fuel (5)

indicatorNotes.at the outset: 'at the outset' means at the start, so only the first letter of 'ruined' is used
indicatorNotes.covered in: something covered in fuel has fuel all round it, so R is wrapped inside COAL

blocks.note: first letter of ruined, placed inside COAL

annotation.surface: A marine reef spoiled from the start by an oil spill.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an oil spill on a reef, which is exactly the answer's scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: coral reefs are among the best-known features of tropical seas.

entries.clue: Republican backing vote for quite some time? (4)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing means supporting from behind, so R stands at the back of the vote

blocks.note: yea is a vote in favour

annotation.surface: A Republican supports a vote that will run for a long while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like a reversal instruction, but R simply comes at the back.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: a year is one stretch that counts as quite some time.

entries.clue: What may indicate rest of Hampshire region? (3,6)

annotation.definitionNote: the rest of the clue is a reverse clue: NEW makes FOREST an anagram of OF REST, so NEW FOREST 'indicates' REST OF

blocks.note: the surface asks what might signal something; the setter means a phrase that, read as a crossword clue, produces it
read the answer as a clue: NEW is an anagram indicator, and FOREST rearranges into REST OF

annotation.surface: A question about what the remainder of Hampshire might be called.
annotation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a national park of heath and woodland in Hampshire, a county in southern England. The clue runs backwards: the answer is itself a tiny clue whose solution is 'rest of'.
annotation.definitionFit: Proper-name definition: the New Forest is a named area within the county of Hampshire.

entries.clue: Possibly flat account: the same, though not in charge (10)

indicatorNotes.though not: 'though not' excludes something, so the letters for in charge are taken out of IDENTICAL

blocks.note: IC = in charge, removed from IDENTICAL

annotation.surface: A bookkeeper describes a flat-rate account that is unchanged but no longer supervised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is musical: an accidental is a sharp, flat or natural sign added to a note, so 'possibly' flags a flat as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example from music notation: a flat sign is one kind of accidental.

entries.clue: Completely exhausted, given ovation on departure? (7-3)

blocks.note: the everyday British slang sense, worn out
the literal reading: applauded as you leave

annotation.surface: A worn-out performer is applauded as they finally leave the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out, usually of a car or machine. The question mark flags the second, literal reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: British slang for worn out, and a whimsical literal one, applauded on the way out.

entries.clue: One’s boring regular practice took effect (5,3)

blocks.note: past tense of bite, as when a rule or a cut bites

annotation.surface: Someone is dull, and their routine exercise has finally worked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One’s boring' reads as someone being dull; it means 'one that is boring', a thing that bores holes.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on boring: not dull but making holes, which is exactly what the cutting tip of a drill does.

entries.clue: Hard avoiding the children in college (4)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so the H is left out
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says the letters are found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters THECH run across 'the ch(ildren)'

annotation.surface: Some pupils at college steer clear of hard work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The children' look like people in the surface; they are just letters to mine.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British abbreviation: a tech is a technical college.

entries.clue: Flying ace destined to be consumed by anger (8)

indicatorNotes.to be consumed by: something consumed is swallowed whole, so the word for destined disappears inside the word for anger

blocks.note: as in 'born to lead', placed inside IRE

annotation.surface: A fighter pilot fated to be eaten up by rage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying ace' reads as one phrase for a fighter pilot; 'Flying' is the definition and 'ace' is just A.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, adjective for adjective: in the air, aloft.

entries.clue: Nine capturing live goat (4)

indicatorNotes.capturing: to capture is to take prisoner and hold, so IX holds BE inside it

annotation.surface: Nine hunters catch a live goat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as the adjective (not dead); it is the verb, to exist.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the ibex is a wild mountain species of goat.

entries.clue: Standard reference point? We align uneasily (4,6)

indicatorNotes.uneasily: something uneasy is unsettled, so the letters of 'align' do not stay in place

blocks.note: the newspaper speaking of itself: we = the Times

annotation.surface: A newspaper uneasily lines up behind an agreed benchmark.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter's paper is the Times, so 'We' can stand for TIMES. A time signal, such as the BBC pips, is a standard against which clocks are set.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition with a question mark: the signal is a reference point for standard time, so 'standard' does double duty.

entries.clue: Upturn in illumination with Greek character here? (6)

annotation.definition: Upturn in illumination with Greek character here?

indicatorNotes.Upturn in: an upturn turns something upward, and in a down clue that means the light word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a source of light; turned up it gives DEL
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

annotation.surface: A place where enlightenment arrives through a Greek figure.
annotation.walkthrough: Delphi was the home of the Greek oracle, so the whole clue also describes it: a place for illumination from a Greek character, the priestess.
annotation.definitionFit: Read whole, the clue describes the oracle's seat: pilgrims came there for illumination from a Greek figure, the Pythia.

entries.clue: Weakened terms in lease when payment ran out (9)

indicatorNotes.terms in: a term is an end or limit, so the terms in 'lease when' are the words' final letters

blocks.note: bled = ran out, as colour or blood does

annotation.surface: The conditions of a tenancy were weakened once the rent ran out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terms' in a lease look like its conditions; here terms are ends, so only the final letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, past participle for past participle: made feeble.

entries.clue: Diver’s first above long drop (5)

indicatorNotes.first: 'first' picks out the opening letter of Diver
indicatorNotes.above: in a down clue, being above means coming earlier, so D sits on top of ITCH

blocks.note: to long for something is to itch for it

annotation.surface: A diver's first plunge from a great height.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long drop' reads as a fall from height; 'long' is the verb yearn, and 'drop' means abandon.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym, verb for verb: to ditch a plan or a partner is to drop it.

entries.clue: Petrol company’s hosting American Rolls (4)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host has guests inside their home, so the company's letters take A in

blocks.note: BP, the oil company, plus the 's

annotation.surface: An oil company is entertaining an American guest in a Rolls-Royce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' suggests the car; baps are soft bread rolls in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional British word: a bap is a soft, flat bread roll.

entries.clue: Refuse to accept study on undetermined quantity (4)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the study comes before Y

blocks.note: a den is a private study
y is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: Someone refuses to accept a study based on an unknown number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as research in the surface; it is a room.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to deny a claim is to reject it as untrue.

entries.clue: Soldiers excessively quiet when crossing furthest part of border (5)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to span it from side to side, so TOOP straddles R
indicatorNotes.furthest part of: the furthest part of a word is its end, so only the last letter of border is used

blocks.note: last letter of border, inside TOOP

annotation.surface: Soldiers keep very quiet as they slip across the far edge of a frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' fits the border scene, but here it means going round R, not over a frontier.
annotation.definitionFit: Collective noun: a troop is a unit of soldiers, especially cavalry.

entries.clue: Revised recent idea, not needing America to act as peacemaker (9)

indicatorNotes.Revised: a revised text is reworked, so the letters are put in a new order
indicatorNotes.not needing: what is not needed can be left out, so the A for America is dropped

annotation.surface: A new plan, dropping the Americans, to broker peace.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one A goes: the other stays in the fodder, which leaves nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: to intercede is to step in between two parties to settle a dispute.

entries.clue: Advanced source of entertainment I found in the French country (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so A, TV and I sit within LA

annotation.surface: A modern entertainment source discovered in France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The French country' suggests France; 'the French' is just LA, and 'country' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one Baltic state.

entries.clue: This reduced each example of criminal behaviour (8)

indicatorNotes.reduced: something reduced is made smaller, so THIS loses its last letter

annotation.surface: This cut every instance of crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This' looks like a pointer to the answer; it is just the fodder for the first chunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: stealing is one particular kind of criminal behaviour.
